# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

## What this is

An internal admin tool (branded "WYR") for managing digital products and sending them to customers. It has three pages: **Virtual Listing** (product CRUD with S3 file storage and emailing download links), **Email History** (a log of every send), and **Key Issuer** (makes license keys for EA/MT4/MT5 products). Express + MySQL backend, React + Vite frontend. Plain JavaScript ES modules everywhere, with no TypeScript.

## Commands

Two separate npm packages: the repo root (backend) and `frontend/`.

```bash
npm run install-all      # npm install in root and frontend/
npm start                # backend (node --watch, :3001) + Vite dev server (:5174) together
npm run server:dev       # backend only, with --watch
npm run client:dev       # frontend only
npm run client:build     # installs frontend deps and builds frontend/dist
npm run server:start     # production: backend also serves frontend/dist
```

There is no linter and no test runner. Tests are standalone `node:assert` scripts: run one with `node <file>`, and it passes if it exits with no output.

```bash
node backend/src/services/keyGenerator.test.mjs
node backend/src/services/emailHistory.test.mjs    # imports the mysql2 pool, so root deps must be installed (no DB connection needed)
node frontend/src/utils/dateTime.test.mjs
node frontend/src/utils/filterListings.test.mjs
```

To check syntax without a test, use `node --check <file>`. When you add a test, name it `*.test.mjs` and put it next to the module it tests.

## Configuration

All config comes from one `.env` at the **repo root** (gitignored). `backend/src/index.js`, `db/connection.js`, and `services/s3.js` each load it by a relative path. Variables: `DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/NAME`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME`, `SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS`, `BACKEND_PORT`, `FRONTEND_PORT`, `NODE_ENV`.

- Set `NODE_ENV=dev` (or `development`) for local work. Otherwise the backend tries to serve `frontend/dist` and prints a warning if it hasn't been built.
- In dev, Vite proxies `/api` to `localhost:3001`, so frontend code always calls relative `/api/...` URLs.
- CORS uses an explicit origin allowlist in `backend/src/index.js`. Add new deployment domains there.

## Database

MySQL. There is no ORM and no migration runner. Routes use `pool.execute` with raw SQL and `?` placeholders.

- `schema.sql` is the base schema (`mysql -u root -p < schema.sql`). Later changes live as dated files in `migrations/` and are applied by hand. `issued_keys` exists **only** in `migrations/2026-09-12-key-issuer.sql`, not in `schema.sql`. When you change the schema, add a new dated migration file.
- The pool uses `timezone: 'Z'` (UTC). The frontend shows timestamps in Singapore time through `frontend/src/utils/dateTime.js`, which treats timestamps with no zone as UTC.
- There is no signup endpoint. You add users by inserting a bcrypt `password_hash` into `users` directly.

## Architecture notes

**Auth is client-side only.** `POST /api/auth/login` checks the bcrypt password and returns the user. The frontend keeps it in `localStorage` (`vl_user`). No session or token exists, and none of the `/api/*` routes check auth.

**Frontend has no router.** `App.jsx` holds the login gate, the sidebar, and an `activePage` state that switches between the listing view (inline in `App.jsx`), `EmailHistoryPage`, and `KeyIssuerPage`. Modals are separate components that `App.jsx` shows through state flags. All styling is in `frontend/src/styles/global.css`, plus inline styles.

**Listings and S3 files** (`routes/listings.js`, `services/s3.js`):
- Uploads use multer memory storage and go to S3 under `listings/<name>_<timestamp><ext>`.
- `file_path` stores the full S3 object URL. `keyFromUrl()` gets the key back only if the URL matches the *currently configured* bucket and region, and returns `null` for anything else.
- When a file is uploaded, the backend overwrites `url_link` with the proxy path `/api/listings/:id/file`. That path redirects to a new presigned URL each time it's opened. `size` and `product_format` are taken from the uploaded file.
- Create and update rewrite user input before storing it. Spaces in `product_name` become `_`. `sku` is split on spaces, the first letter of each word is lowercased, and the words are joined with `_`.
- Replacing or deleting a listing also deletes its S3 object.

**Sending** (`routes/send.js`): this builds presigned download URLs that last 3 days and an inline-styled HTML email with the logo embedded by CID from `backend/static/`, then sends it with nodemailer. The MT4/MT5 import-guide PDFs from `backend/static/` are attached when a product name contains both `ea` and `mt4`/`mt5` (a substring match, case-insensitive). Every send first writes an `email_history` row with status `pending` and a snapshot of each product in `email_history_items`, then sets the status to `sent` or `failed` with the error message (`services/emailHistory.js`).

**Key Issuer** (`services/keyGenerator.js`): a port of a legacy WinForms "MYR Key Issuer" app. `outputKey = "FF" + yyyyMMdd + last 4 bytes of MD5(hex bytes of "FF"+expiry+hardwareId)`. The downloadable `ap.dc` file is those 5 prefix bytes followed by the full 16-byte MD5 digest. The test pins exact outputs from the legacy app, so the derivation must stay byte-for-byte compatible. The download endpoint rebuilds the file from the stored `hardware_id` and `expiry_date`.

## Docs

`docs/superpowers/plans/` contains implementation plans written for the superpowers workflow skills. Follow the same format for new multi-step features.

# CLAUDE.md

## What this is

## Commands

Two separate npm packages: the repo root (backend) and `frontend/`.

```bash
npm run install-all      # npm install in root and frontend/
npm start                # backend (node --watch, :3001) + Vite dev server (:5174) together
npm run server:dev       # backend only, with --watch
npm run client:dev       # frontend only
npm run client:build     # installs frontend deps and builds frontend/dist
npm run server:start     # production: backend also serves frontend/dist
```

There is no linter and no test runner. Tests are standalone `node:assert` scripts: run one with `node <file>`, and it passes if it exits with no output.

```bash
node backend/src/services/keyGenerator.test.mjs
node backend/src/services/emailHistory.test.mjs    # imports the mysql2 pool, so root deps must be installed (no DB connection needed)
node frontend/src/utils/dateTime.test.mjs
node frontend/src/utils/filterListings.test.mjs
```

To check syntax without a test, use `node --check <file>`. When you add a test, name it `*.test.mjs` and put it next to the module it tests.

## Configuration

All config comes from one `.env` at the **repo root** (gitignored). `backend/src/index.js`, `db/connection.js`, and `services/s3.js` each load it by a relative path. - Set `NODE_ENV=dev` (or `development`) for local work. Otherwise the backend tries to serve `frontend/dist` and prints a warning if it hasn't been built.
- In dev, Vite proxies `/api` to `localhost:3001`, so frontend code always calls relative `/api/...` URLs.
- CORS uses an explicit origin allowlist in `backend/src/index.js`. Add new deployment domains there.

## Configuration

All config comes from one `.env` at the **repo root** (gitignored). `backend/src/index.js`, `db/connection.js`, and `services/s3.js` each load it by a relative path. Variables: `DB_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD/NAME`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME`, `SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS`, `BACKEND_PORT`, `FRONTEND_PORT`, `NODE_ENV`.

- Set `NODE_ENV=dev` (or `development`) for local work. Otherwise the backend tries to serve `frontend/dist` and prints a warning if it hasn't been built.
- In dev, Vite proxies `/api` to `localhost:3001`, so frontend code always calls relative `/api/...` URLs.
- CORS uses an explicit origin allowlist in `backend/src/index.js`. Add new deployment domains there.

## Database

MySQL. There is no ORM and no migration runner. Routes use `pool.execute` with raw SQL and `?` placeholders.

- `schema.sql` is the base schema (`mysql -u root -p < schema.sql`). Later changes live as dated files in `migrations/` and are applied by hand. Some tables exist **only** in a migration, not in `schema.sql`: `issued_keys` (`migrations/2026-09-12-key-issuer.sql`), `card_copy_orders` (`migrations/2026-09-13-card-copy.sql`), and `card_copy_read_requests` (`migrations/2026-09-14-card-copy-read-requests.sql`). When you change the schema, add a new dated migration file.
- The pool uses `timezone: 'Z'` (UTC). The frontend shows timestamps in Singapore time through `frontend/src/utils/dateTime.js`, which treats timestamps with no zone as UTC.
- There is no signup endpoint. You add users by inserting a bcrypt `password_hash` into `users` directly.

## Architecture notes

**Auth is client-side only.** `POST /api/auth/login` checks the bcrypt password and returns the user. The frontend keeps it in `localStorage` (`vl_user`). No session or token exists, and none of the `/api/*` routes check auth.

**Frontend has no router.** `App.jsx` holds the login gate, the sidebar, and an `activePage` state that switches between the listing view (inline in `App.jsx`), `EmailHistoryPage`, and `KeyIssuerPage`. Modals are separate components that `App.jsx` shows through state flags. All styling is in `frontend/src/styles/global.css`, plus inline styles.

**Listings and S3 files** (`routes/listings.js`, `services/s3.js`):
- Uploads use multer memory storage and go to S3 under `listings/<name>_<timestamp><ext>`.
- `file_path` stores the full S3 object URL. `keyFromUrl()` gets the key back only if the URL matches the *currently configured* bucket and region, and returns `null` for anything else.
- When a file is uploaded, the backend overwrites `url_link` with the proxy path `/api/listings/:id/file`. That path redirects to a new presigned URL each time it's opened. `size` and `product_format` are taken from the uploaded file.
- Create and update rewrite user input before storing it. Spaces in `product_name` become `_`. `sku` is split on spaces, the first letter of each word is lowercased, and the words are joined with `_`.
- Replacing or deleting a listing also deletes its S3 object.

**Sending** (`routes/send.js`): this builds presigned download URLs that last 3 days and an inline-styled HTML email with the logo embedded by CID from `backend/static/`, then sends it with nodemailer. The MT4/MT5 import-guide PDFs from `backend/static/` are attached when a product name contains both `ea` and `mt4`/`mt5` (a substring match, case-insensitive). Every send first writes an `email_history` row with status `pending` and a snapshot of each product in `email_history_items`, then sets the status to `sent` or `failed` with the error message (`services/emailHistory.js`).

**Card Copy Program** (`routes/cardCopy.js` + `services/cardCopy*.js`): a port of the `CloneCardSellerProgram` C# WinForms app. The operator pastes a client's RFID memory-bank dump (Order ID + Data A–E = Reserved/EPC/TID/User/DateTime), which is parsed (`cardCopyParser.js`) and run through TID chip identification (`cardCopyTidParser.js`). On approve, the backend recomputes a verification hash and an **AES-256-CBC encrypted `BEGIN_SELLER_DATA…END_SELLER_DATA` blob** (`cardCopyCrypto.js`) for the client to decrypt. **`cardCopyCrypto.js` must stay byte-compatible with the desktop app** — same passphrase (zero-padded to 32 bytes), AES-256-CBC/PKCS7, `base64(IV+ciphertext)` then base64 again inside the wrapper, and the same SHA-256 checksum/hash construction — or existing client programs can no longer decrypt it. `cardCopyCrypto.test.mjs` locks the round-trip and checksum. Orders are upserted by `order_id` (`cardCopyOrders.js`), replacing the desktop app's local JSON file.

**Mykad Key Issuer** (`services/keyGenerator.js`): a port of a legacy WinForms "MYR Key Issuer" app. `outputKey = "FF" + yyyyMMdd + last 4 bytes of MD5(hex bytes of "FF"+expiry+hardwareId)`. The downloadable `ap.dc` file is those 5 prefix bytes followed by the full 16-byte MD5 digest. The test pins exact outputs from the legacy app, so the derivation must stay byte-for-byte compatible. The download endpoint rebuilds the file from the stored `hardware_id` and `expiry_date`.
